note: GH-001 discover repository channel: src/channels/discovery.zig resolves a user-style repository URL by fetching a pinned descriptor, recording the revision the client read, and deciding trust afterwards as its own step. The two facts are kept apart on purpose: a descriptor that was fetched has a real revision even when its signature is wrong, and an operator needs to know whether they are looking at the wrong document or at a forgery of the right one, so the revision is recorded first and returned alongside the trust decision rather than being replaced by it. An unknown key is a third answer again, not a synonym for an invalid signature. Writing the module exposed a design flaw in my first draft: a signature cannot cover a document that contains it, so the signed bytes are now an explicit canonical payload rendered from the descriptor's fields, which is what makes verifying a document that arrived over an untrusted transport possible at all. The fixture serves the forged document over the same real HTTP transport as the honest one. Fault proof: assuming trust instead of deciding it makes the forged-descriptor assertion fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
